title: What did I change?

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: I cannot remember what I typed in the schedule earlier. Can you check?

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: `git diff` shows changes that are **not** staged yet.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: `git diff --staged` shows changes that **are** staged, waiting for the next commit.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Two different questions, two different commands. Run both and compare.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Lines starting with `+` were added. Lines starting with `-` were removed.

items.text: Look at the unstaged changes with git diff
Answer: which line is only in the working folder?
Answer: which change is already staged?

questions.prompt: Run `git diff`. Which line does it show as added?
questions.explanation: Dumplings was typed after `git add`, so it is unstaged. `git diff` shows exactly that.

questions.prompt: Now run `git diff --staged`. What is waiting to be committed?

choices.text: The closing time, and the first version of the menu

questions.explanation: You staged the closing time and the Noodles line earlier. `--staged` shows what the next commit would contain.

recap: `git diff` shows what is not staged yet. `git diff --staged` shows what is staged for the next commit.

cheatSheet.summary: See changes you have not staged
See changes that are staged for the next commit

hints: There are two diffs to look at: one for unstaged changes, one for staged changes.
`git diff` shows unstaged work. `git diff --staged` shows what you already added.
Run `git diff`, then run `git diff --staged`, then answer both questions.
